data.title: Adex Mining Announces Adjournment of Appeal Before New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board
data.description:
Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - Adex Mining Inc.  ("Adex" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that Adex Minerals Corp. ("Adex Minerals"), the Company's wholly-owned subsidiary through which Adex holds its interest in the Mount Pleasant mining project in New Brunswick, has agreed jointly with the Mining Recorder, Resource and Development Branch of the New Brunswick Department of Natural Resources and Energy (the "Mining Recorder") to adjourn the Appeal (as defined below) previously announced by Adex and originally scheduled to proceed before the New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board (the "NBEUB") on December 3 and 4, 2026. The formal hearing is now scheduled to take place on March 11 and 12, 2027. The decision to adjourn the Appeal was made jointly and by mutual consent with counsel for the Mining Recorder. The adjournment will allow the Company to focus its efforts and internal resources on achieving a successful outcome to its ongoing strategic review process through including identifying and executing a value-maximizing transaction for Adex in respect of the Mount Pleasant project.

As previously disclosed in its press releases dated July 29, 2026 and September 10, 2026, Adex Minerals received correspondence dated July 13, 2026 from the Mining Recorder advising that the mineral claim 1505 (the "Mineral Claim" upon which the Mount Pleasant project is situated) had been cancelled by the Mining Recorder and placed in protected status due to failures by Adex Minerals to complete sufficient work program expenditures as required under s. 11(1) of the General Regulation - Mining Act, N.B. Reg. 86-98. Adex Minerals appealed this decision on July 29, 2026 (the "Appeal"). On September 9, 2026, after an interim stay hearing conducted before the NBEUB on August 31, 2026, Adex Minerals successfully obtained an interim stay of the Mining Recorder's cancellation of the Mineral Claim, and the Mineral Claim was reinstated in the name of Adex Minerals pending a final determination of the Appeal. This status remains in effect pending the newly-rescheduled Appeal hearing.

The adjournment does not reflect any concession on the part of the Company, and the Company remains confident in its position on, and is optimistic of a favourable result in, the hearing of the Appeal. Adex Minerals continues to believe that the Mining Recorder failed to engage with Adex Minerals' good faith proposals to complete the necessary expenditures in a timely manner and acted unreasonably in imposing arbitrary deadlines after eschewing Adex Minerals' good faith efforts to comply. Adex's special committee of independent directors continues to work with its external advisors and remains fully engaged in pursuing potential transaction opportunities with interested parties in accordance with its ongoing mandate previously described by the Company.

ABOUT ADEX

Adex Mining Inc. is a Canadian junior mining company with an experienced management team. The Company has maintained stewardship over the Mount Pleasant property while evaluating strategic alternatives. The Mount Pleasant property is a multi-metal project that is host to promising tungsten-molybdenum and tin-indium-zinc mineralization. The common shares of Adex trade on the TSX Venture Exchange under the stock symbol "ADE".

data.title: IPOs Struggle in Tech Selloff. Berkshire Has a Winner. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

The old investment adage to avoid initial public offerings has held up this year, as many stocks are trading well below their IPO prices.

Barron's looked at 18 companies that made their U.S. stock-market debuts in 2026, including marquee offerings like SpaceX, Cerebras Systems, Innio, Madison Air Solutions and Jersey Mike's, found that 15 of them are below their offering prices. Many are down 50% or more.

SK Hynix, already public in South Korea, made its U.S. debut in July through an offering of American depositary shares. That stock also is trading below its U.S. offering price in July.

Why do IPOs often falter? Companies that come public often are in hot industries, and carry high valuations to reflect investor optimism. That enthusiasm often wanes, however. This year, some deals were keyed off the AI buildout and enthusiasm for that trend has faded.

There are some winners, notably Arxis, a defense contractor with an aerospace focus; Pershing Square, Bill Ackman's investment management company, and Bending Spoons, the rollup of mature tech companies like AOL.

Give Berkshire Hathaway some credit. The company headed now by CEO Greg Abel picked the right deal when it invested $600 million in Bending Spoons at the July IPO at $29 a share. The stock traded recently at $45, up 55%. In October, Berkshire bought another $330 million of stock at $33.

Berkshire rarely buys IPOs — reflecting former CEO Warren Buffett's well-founded aversion to them. It participated in Snowflake's IPO in 2020.

Looking at some of the larger deals, SpaceX trades around $131, against an IPO price of $135; Cerebras at $82, less than half its IPO price of $185; and SK Hynix at $124, versus its U.S. offering price of $149.

One of the better ways to play IPOs in a diversified way is through the Renaissance IPO ETF. It adds newly public companies every three months as part of a regular rebalancing and companies cycle out after three years. Individual holdings are capped at a 10% weighting at rebalancing.

Its largest holdings now are SpaceX at nearly 10%, followed by SK Hynix and Astera Labs, both at more than 7%. The ETF, now around $45, is off about 2% so far this year.

Be careful about SK Hynix ADRs. While chip stocks have come under pressure, SK Hynix's U.S. shares trade at a big premium to the Korean shares that Barron's estimates is close to 50%.

Busted IPOs also can be a good place to look for values, and there are many companies to comb through this year.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

data.title: Canadian dollar posts steepest decline since January on surprise jobs loss
data.description:
By Fergal Smith

The Canadian dollar fell by the most in nine months against its US counterpart on Friday after domestic data showed the economy shed jobs for a third straight month, cooling expectations for Bank of Canada interest rate hikes.

The loonie was trading 0.8% lower at 1.4128 per US dollar, or 70.78 US cents, after touching its weakest intraday level since October 19 at 1.4137. It was the steepest daily decline for the currency since January 30.

  • For the week, the currency was down 1.1%, after three straight weeks of gains, as equity markets globally were buffeted by a selloff in AI stocks.

  • "The CAD has failed to deliver on the potential for its recent rebound to extend this week," Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret, FX strategists at Scotiabank, said in a note.

  • "Elevated equity-market volatility has overshadowed pretty much everything else, although the combination of weak Canadian and strong US jobs data has given the CAD an added nudge lower into the weekend," the strategists said.

  • Canadian employment fell 4,700 in October and the jobless rate rose to a six-month high of 6.7%. Analysts had expected a 13,600 jobs gain.

  • Chances the Bank of Canada would tighten in December dipped to 36% from 40%, swap market data showed.

  • The Canadian central bank unveiled on Thursday a new five-year monetary policy framework with the federal finance ministry, keeping its inflation target unchanged at 2%.

  • Also on Thursday, Prime Minister Mark Carney's budget showed that he plans to use windfall oil revenue to boost Canada's productivity and build infrastructure while keeping his previous fiscal goals intact.

  • US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October, boosting the US dollar against a basket of major currencies.

  • US crude futures CLc1 posted a steep weekly decline after the election losses of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party raised hopes of a de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran. Oil is one of Canada's major exports.

  • The Canadian 2-year yield (CA2YT=RR) was down one basis points at 3.146%, while it fell 4.5 basis points further below the equivalent US rate to a gap of about 137 basis points.
